are as desired.
∎

4.8.
Bicolourisation

It remains to argue that by taking a random preimage we can convert
Corollary
4.20
into Proposition
2.6
.

Proof of Proposition
2.6
.

Given
\varepsilon
and
t
we take
\gamma,\mu>0
and
\ell\in\mathds{N}
such that

\gamma=\frac{\varepsilon}{12}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\varepsilon,t^{-1}\gg\ell^{-1}\gg\mu

and consider an
\varepsilon
-wicked reduced hypergraph
\mathcal{A}
whose index set
I

is sufficiently large.
Due to Corollary
4.20
there are a set
J\subseteq I
of size
t

and
\varepsilon
-disjoint
\mu
-holes
\Phi
,
\Psi
on
J
such that
for all
i<j<k
in
J
we have

(4.33)

|{\mathscr{B}}^{ijk}(\Phi,\Psi,\gamma)|\leq\mu|\mathcal{P}^{ij}||\mathcal{P}^{ik}|\,,\quad|{\mathscr{C}}^{ijk}(\Phi,\Psi,\gamma)|\leq\mu|\mathcal{P}^{ij}||\mathcal{P}^{jk}|\,,\\
\text{and}\quad|{\mathscr{D}}^{ijk}(\Phi,\Psi,\gamma)|\leq\mu|\mathcal{P}^{ik}||\mathcal{P}^{jk}|\,.

Next we define a reduced subhypergraph
\mathcal{A}_{1}
of
\mathcal{A}
admitting a bicolouring
\varphi_{1}

which satisfies, with only few exceptions, the minimum codegree
condition
\tau_{2}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\varphi_{1})\geq 1/3+\varepsilon/4
. To this end we consider for every
pair
ij\in J^{(2)}
the sets

\mathfrak{R}^{ij}=\Phi^{ij}\smallsetminus\Psi^{ij}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathfrak{B}^{ij}=\Psi^{ij}\smallsetminus\Phi^{ij}\,,

and then we set
\mathfrak{R}=\mathop{\vphantom{\bigcup}\mathchoice{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\displaystyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\textstyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\scriptstyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\scriptscriptstyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}}\displaylimits_{ij\in J^{(2)}}\mathfrak{R}^{ij}

as well as
\mathfrak{B}=\mathop{\vphantom{\bigcup}\mathchoice{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\displaystyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\textstyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\scriptstyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\scriptscriptstyle#$\hfil\cr\bigcup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}}\displaylimits_{ij\in J^{(2)}}\mathfrak{B}^{ij}
.
Now let
\mathcal{A}_{1}
be the reduced hypergraph with index set
J
, vertex
classes
\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ij}=\mathfrak{R}^{ij}\mathbin{\mathchoice{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\displaystyle#$\hfil\cr\cup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\textstyle#$\hfil\cr\cup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\scriptstyle#$\hfil\cr\cup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}{\vtop{\halign{\hfil$\m@th\scriptscriptstyle#$\hfil\cr\cup\cr\cdot\crcr}}}}\mathfrak{B}^{ij}\subseteq\mathcal{P}^{ij}
for every
ij\in J^{(2)}
, and edges

E(\mathcal{A}_{1})=E(\mathfrak{R}\cup\mathfrak{B})\smallsetminus\bigl(E(\mathfrak{R})\cup E(\mathfrak{B})\bigr)\,.

Since
\Phi
and
\Psi
are
\varepsilon
-disjoint and have width at least
1/3+\varepsilon
we have

(4.34)

\big|\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ij}\big|\geq\Big(\frac{2}{3}+\varepsilon\Big)\big|\mathcal{P}^{ij}\big|

for every
ij\in J^{(2)}
.

It is plain that the map
\varphi_{1}\colon V(\mathcal{A}_{1})\longrightarrow\{\textrm{red},\textrm{blue}\}

defined by
\varphi_{1}^{-1}(\textrm{red})=\mathfrak{R}
and
\varphi_{1}^{-1}(\textrm{blue})=\mathfrak{B}
is
a bicolouring of
\mathcal{A}_{1}
.

Claim 4.21
.

In
\mathcal{A}_{1}
all monochromatic cherries
(P_{1}^{ij},P_{1}^{ik})

that fail to be
\gamma
-bad in
\mathcal{A}
have codegree at least
(1/3+\varepsilon/4)|\mathcal{P}_{1}^{jk}|
.

Proof.

Suppose
i<j<k

and that
(P_{1}^{ij},P_{1}^{ik})=(R^{ij},R^{ik})\in\mathfrak{R}^{ij}\times\mathfrak{R}^{ik}

is a red left cherry not belonging to
{\mathscr{B}}^{ijk}(\Phi,\Psi,\gamma)
.
Due to

|N_{\mathcal{A}}(R^{ij},R^{ik})\smallsetminus\Psi^{jk}|\leq\gamma|\mathcal{P}^{jk}|

we have

\displaystyle|N_{\mathcal{A}_{1}}(R^{ij},R^{ik})|

\displaystyle=\!|N_{\mathcal{A}}(R^{ij},R^{ik})\cap\mathfrak{B}^{jk}|

\displaystyle\geq\!|N_{\mathcal{A}}(R^{ij},R^{ik})|-|N_{\mathcal{A}}(R^{ij},R^{ik})\smallsetminus\Psi^{jk}|-|\Phi^{jk}\cap\Psi^{jk}|

\displaystyle\geq\!\left(\frac{1}{3}+\varepsilon\right)|\mathcal{P}^{jk}|-\gamma|\mathcal{P}^{jk}|-|\Phi^{jk}\cap\Psi^{jk}|

\displaystyle\geq\!\left(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right)\left(|\mathcal{P}^{jk}|-|\Phi^{jk}\cap\Psi^{jk}|\right)+\frac{2}{3}\left(\varepsilon|\mathcal{P}^{jk}|-|\Phi^{jk}\cap\Psi^{jk}|\right)

\displaystyle\geq\!\left(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right)|\mathcal{P}_{1}^{jk}|\,,

where the penultimate inequality uses the definition of
\gamma
and
the last inequality follows
from
\mathcal{P}_{1}^{jk}\subseteq\mathcal{P}^{jk}\smallsetminus(\Phi^{jk}\cap\Psi^{jk})
.
This concludes the proof for red left cherries and all other cases can
be treated analogously.
∎

Similarly as in
[
16
]
*Lemma 4.2 we will define the
reduced hypergraph
\mathcal{A}_{\star}
by taking the preimage of a random homomorphism

h\in\mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ell)
. Recall from Definition
3.5

that for every map
h\in\mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ell)
the
associated reduced hypergraph
\mathcal{A}_{h}
has index set
J
and vertex classes

\mathcal{P}_{\bullet}^{ij}
of size
\ell
.

Observe that there is no
h\in\mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ell)
such that
\mathcal{A}_{h}
supports a
K_{5}^{(3)}
,
because otherwise the homomorphism
h
would show that
\mathcal{A}_{1}\subseteq\mathcal{A}

supports a
K_{5}^{(3)}
as well, contrary to
\mathcal{A}
being wicked.
Furthermore, for every
h\in\mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ell)
the map
\varphi_{h}=\varphi_{1}\circ h
is
a bicolouring of
\mathcal{A}_{h}
. So it remains to show that if
h
gets chosen uniformly
at random, then with positive probability the event

\tau_{2}(\mathcal{A}_{h},\varphi_{h})\geq\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\varepsilon}{8}

occurs. We estimate for each cherry of
\mathcal{A}_{h}
the probability that it violates
this condition.

Claim 4.22
.

If
ijk\in J^{(3)}
and
(P_{\bullet}^{ij},P_{\bullet}^{ik})\in\mathcal{P}_{\bullet}^{ij}\times\mathcal{P}_{\bullet}^{ik}

is a cherry of
\mathcal{A}_{h}
, then
the event
{\mathcal{X}}
that

\varphi_{h}(P_{\bullet}^{ij})=\varphi_{h}(P_{\bullet}^{ik})\quad\text{and}\quad|N_{\mathcal{A}_{h}}(P_{\bullet}^{ij},P_{\bullet}^{ik})|<\Big(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\varepsilon}{8}\Big)|\mathcal{P}_{\bullet}^{jk}|

has at most the probability
3\mu+\exp\big({-}\tfrac{\varepsilon^{2}\ell}{128}\big)
.

Proof.

Without loss of generality we may assume
i<j<k
. By the law of total probability we have

\mathds{P}({\mathcal{X}})=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ij}||\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ik}|}\sum_{(P^{ij},P^{ik})\in\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ij}\times\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ik}}\mathds{P}\left({\mathcal{X}}\,\big|\,h(P_{\bullet}^{ij})=P^{ij}\ \text{and}\ h(P_{\bullet}^{ik})=P^{ik}\right)\,.

Note that cherries
(P^{ij},P^{ik})
consisting of two vertices with different
colours contribute zero to this sum. Moreover, due to (
4.33
) the total
contribution from cherries
(P^{ij},P^{ik})
belonging
to
{\mathscr{B}}^{ijk}(\Phi,\Psi,\gamma)

is at most

\frac{\mu|\mathcal{P}^{ij}||\mathcal{P}^{ik}|}{|\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ij}||\mathcal{P}_{1}^{ik}|}\overset{\eqref{eq:sP1}}{\leq}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2}\mu<3\mu\,.

Furthermore, for
P^{ij}
,
P^{ik}
of the
same colour with
(P^{ij},P^{ik})\not\in{\mathscr{B}}^{ijk}(\Phi,\Psi,\gamma)

Claim
4.21
combined with Chernoff’s inequality tells us

\mathds{P}\left({\mathcal{X}}\,\big|\,h(P_{\bullet}^{ij})=P^{ij}\ \text{and}\ h(P_{\bullet}^{ik})=P^{ik}\right)\leq\exp\big({-}\tfrac{\varepsilon^{2}\ell}{128}\big)

and Claim
4.22
follows.
∎

Since
\mathcal{A}_{h}
has
3\ell^{2}\binom{t}{3}
cherries, Claim
4.22
implies

\displaystyle\mathds{P}\left(\tau_{2}(\mathcal{A}_{h},\varphi_{h})<\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\varepsilon}{8}\right)\leq 3\ell^{2}\binom{t}{3}\left(3\mu+\exp\big({-}\tfrac{\varepsilon^{2}\ell}{128}\big)\right)\,.

Owing to the hierarchy
\mu\ll\ell^{-1}\ll t^{-1}
this probability is smaller
than
1
and, therefore, there is a map
h\in\mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ell)
for which
\mathcal{A}_{h}
has the desired properties.
∎

5.
Cliques on five vertices in bicoloured reduced hypergraphs

In this section we establish Proposition
2.7
and show that bicoloured reduced hypergraphs with minimum monochromatic codegree density bigger than
1/3
support a
K_{5}^{(3)}
.

In the proof we shall use the following types of neighbourhoods in reduced hypergraphs
\mathcal{A}
.
For two vertices
P
,
P^{\prime}\in V(\mathcal{A})
and a subset
{\mathcal{U}}\subseteq V(\mathcal{A})
we denote by
N_{{\mathcal{U}}}(P,P^{\prime})
the neighbourhood restricted to
{\mathcal{U}}
. Similarly, for two subsets

{\mathcal{U}}
,
{\mathcal{U}}^{\prime}\subseteq V(\mathcal{A})
we write
N_{{\mathcal{U}}\times{\mathcal{U}}^{\prime}}(P)
for the set of
pairs in
{\mathcal{U}}\times{\mathcal{U}}^{\prime}
that together with
P
form a hyperedge in
\mathcal{A}
, i.e.,

\displaystyle N_{{\mathcal{U}}}(P,P^{\prime})

\displaystyle=\{U\in{\mathcal{U}}\colon PP^{\prime}U\in E(\mathcal{A})\}

\displaystyle\quad\text{and}\quad N_{{\mathcal{U}}\times{\mathcal{U}}^{\prime}}(P)

\displaystyle=\{(U,U^{\prime})\in{\mathcal{U}}\times{\mathcal{U}}^{\prime}\colon PUU^{\prime}\in E(\mathcal{A})\}\,.

Proof of Proposition
2.7
.

Clearly we may assume that
\varepsilon<\frac{1}{6}
.
Fix a sufficiently small auxiliary constant
\xi
with
0<\xi\ll\varepsilon

such that
\frac{1/6-\varepsilon}{\xi}
is equal to some positive integer
s
.
Moreover, let
I
be a sufficiently large index set such that its cardinality
satisfies the partition relation
|I|\longrightarrow(5)^{2}_{s}
, meaning that it is at least
as large as the
s
-colour Ramsey number for the graph clique
K_{5}
.
Let
\mathcal{A}
be a bicoloured reduced hypergraph with index set
I
and vertex
classes
\mathcal{P}^{ij}
for
ij\in I^{(2)}
and let the bicolouring

\varphi\colon V(\mathcal{A})\longrightarrow\{\textrm{red},\textrm{blue}\}
satisfy
\tau_{2}(\mathcal{A},\varphi)\geq 1/3+\varepsilon
.

For every
ij\in I^{(2)}
we set

\mathfrak{R}^{ij}=\varphi^{-1}(\textrm{red})\cap\mathcal{P}^{ij}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\varrho_{ij}=\frac{|\mathfrak{R}^{ij}|}{|\mathcal{P}^{ij}|}

and, analogously, we define
\mathfrak{B}^{ij}=\varphi^{-1}(\textrm{blue})\cap\mathcal{P}^{ij}
and

\beta_{ij}=|\mathfrak{B}^{ij}|/|\mathcal{P}^{ij}|
.
In view of (
2.1
), the assumption on
\tau_{2}(\mathcal{A},\varphi)

implies that all
\varrho_{ij}
,
\beta_{ij}
are in
[1/3+\varepsilon,2/3-\varepsilon]
.
Splitting this interval into
s
intervals of length
2\xi
, the size of
I
yields a subset
J\subseteq I
of size
5
such that all
\beta_{ij}
with
ij\in J^{(2)}
are in the same interval.
Let
\beta
be the centre of this interval and set
\varrho=1-\beta
. We thus arrive at

\beta_{ij}=\beta\pm\xi\qquad\text{and}\qquad\varrho_{ij}=\varrho\pm\xi

for all
ij\in J^{(2)}
.
Without loss of generality we may assume
\beta\leq\varrho
, which implies

(5.1)

\displaystyle\frac{1}{3}+\varepsilon\leq\beta-\xi<\beta\leq\frac{1}{2}\leq\varrho<\varrho+\xi\leq\frac{2}{3}-\varepsilon\,.

For
ijk\in J^{(3)}
the codegree condition translates for
red
vertices
R^{ij}\in\mathfrak{R}^{ij}

and
R^{ik}\in\mathfrak{R}^{ik}
to

\displaystyle|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{jk}}(R^{ij},R^{ik})|=d(R^{ij},R^{jk})

\displaystyle\geq\left(\frac{1}{3}+\varepsilon\right)|\mathcal{P}^{jk}|

(5.2)

\displaystyle\geq\left(\frac{1}{3}+\varepsilon\right)\left(\frac{1}{\beta+\xi}\right)|\mathfrak{B}^{jk}|\geq\left(\frac{1}{3\beta}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)|\mathfrak{B}^{jk}|\,,

where we used
\xi\ll\varepsilon,\beta
for the last inequality. Similarly, for
blue
vertices we have

(5.3)

|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{jk}}(B^{ij},B^{ik})|\geq\left(\frac{1}{3\varrho}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)|\mathfrak{R}^{jk}|\,.

We may rename the indices in
J
and assume that
J=\mathds{Z}/5\mathds{Z}
.
We shall show that
\mathcal{A}
restricted to
J
supports a
K_{5}^{(3)}
. For that we have to find
ten vertices
P^{ij}\in\mathcal{P}^{ij}
, one for every
ij\in J^{(2)}
, such that for all of the ten triples

ijk\in J^{(3)}
the vertices
P^{ij}
,
P^{ik}
, and
P^{jk}
span a hyperedge in the constituent
\mathcal{A}^{ijk}
. For every
i\in J=\mathds{Z}/5\mathds{Z}
we will select
P^{i,i+1}
from
\mathfrak{B}^{i,i+1}

and
P^{i,i+2}
from
\mathfrak{R}^{i,i+2}
.
Since
\mathcal{A}
contains no monochromatic triples as hyperedges, this choice for the colour classes is up to a permutation of indices unavoidable, as it corresponds to the unique
2
-colouring of
E(K_{5})
with no monochromatic triangle.

The rest of the proof is based on several averaging arguments relying on the minimum degree condition.
For generic vertices from
\mathfrak{R}
and
\mathfrak{B}
we shall use capital letters
R
and
B
. In the process,
we will make appropriate choices to fix the ten special vertices that induce the
supported
K_{5}^{(3)}
. For those vertices, we will use small letters
r
and
b
depending on their colour.

We begin with the selection of
r^{14}\in\mathfrak{R}^{14}
.
Applying (
5.3
) to all pairs of vertices
B^{15}\in\mathfrak{B}^{15}
and
B^{45}\in\mathfrak{B}^{45}

implies that the total number of hyperedges in
\mathcal{A}^{145}

crossing the sets
\mathfrak{R}^{14}
,
\mathfrak{B}^{15}
, and
\mathfrak{B}^{45}
is at least

|\mathfrak{B}^{15}||\mathfrak{B}^{45}|\cdot\left(\frac{1}{3\varrho}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)|\mathfrak{R}^{14}|\,.

Consequently, we can fix some vertex
r^{14}\in\mathfrak{R}^{14}
such that

(5.4)

\displaystyle|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{15}\times\mathfrak{B}^{45}}(r^{14})|\geq\left(\frac{1}{3\varrho}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)|\mathfrak{B}^{15}||\mathfrak{B}^{45}|\,.

The following claim fixes the four vertices
b^{12}
,
b^{34}
and
r^{13}
,
r^{24}
.

Claim 5.1
.

There are blue vertices
b^{12}\in\mathfrak{B}^{12}
,
b^{34}\in\mathfrak{B}^{34}

and red vertices
r^{13}\in\mathfrak{R}^{13}
,
{r^{24}\in\mathfrak{R}^{24}}
such that

(

)

b^{12}r^{14}r^{24}
and
r^{13}r^{14}b^{34}
are hyperedges in
\mathcal{A}

(

)

and
|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(b^{12},r^{13})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})|\geq\bigl(1-\frac{1}{3\beta}\bigr)|\mathfrak{B}^{23}|
.

Proof.

Owing to (
5.2
) for every
R^{13}\in\mathfrak{R}^{13}
we have

d(R^{13},r^{14})\geq\big(\frac{1}{3\beta}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\big)|\mathfrak{B}^{34}|

and, hence, there is a vertex
b^{34}\in\mathfrak{B}^{34}
such that

(5.5)

\displaystyle|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})|\geq\left(\frac{1}{3\beta}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)|\mathfrak{R}^{13}|\geq\frac{\varrho}{3\beta}|\mathcal{P}^{13}|\,.

Similarly, we can fix a vertex
r^{24}\in\mathfrak{R}^{24}
such that

(5.6)

\displaystyle|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})|\geq\frac{1}{3\varrho}|\mathfrak{B}^{23}|\,.

Recalling that
|\mathfrak{R}^{13}|\leq(\varrho+\xi)|\mathcal{P}^{13}|
for every
B^{12}\in\mathfrak{B}^{12}
and
B^{23}\in\mathfrak{B}^{23}
we have

\displaystyle\big|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(B^{12},B^{23})\cap N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})\big|

\displaystyle\overset{\phantom{\eqref{eq:13}}}{\geq}\left(\frac{1}{3}+\varepsilon\right)|\mathcal{P}^{13}|+\big|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})\big|-|\mathfrak{R}^{13}|

\displaystyle\overset{\phantom{\eqref{eq:13}}}{\geq}\big|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})\big|-\left(\varrho+\xi-\frac{1}{3}-\varepsilon\right)|\mathcal{P}^{13}|

\displaystyle\overset{\eqref{eq:13}}{\geq}\left(1-3\beta+\frac{\beta}{\varrho}\right)\big|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})\big|

\displaystyle\overset{\phantom{\eqref{eq:13}}}{\geq}\left(3\varrho-\frac{\varrho}{\beta}\right)\big|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})\big|\,,

where the last estimate uses
\beta+\varrho=1
and
\frac{\beta}{\varrho}+\frac{\varrho}{\beta}\geq 2
.
Hence, the number of hyperedges crossing
N_{\mathfrak{B}^{12}}(r^{14},r^{24})
,

N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})
, and
N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})
is at least

|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{12}}(r^{14},r^{24})||N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})|\cdot\left(3\varrho-\frac{\varrho}{\beta}\right)|N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})|\,.

Consequently, there exist
b^{12}\in N_{\mathfrak{B}^{12}}(r^{14},r^{24})

and
r^{13}\in N_{\mathfrak{R}^{13}}(r^{14},b^{34})
such that

\displaystyle|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(b^{12},r^{13})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})|

\displaystyle\overset{\phantom{\eqref{eq:23}}}{\geq}\left(3\varrho-\frac{\varrho}{\beta}\right)|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})|

\displaystyle\overset{\eqref{eq:23}}{\geq}\left(1-\frac{1}{3\beta}\right)|\mathfrak{B}^{23}|\,.\qed

The next claim fixes the four vertices
b^{15}
,
b^{45}
and
r^{25}
,
r^{35}
. Together with Claim
5.1

this fixes all vertices except
b^{23}
and both claims together guarantee those seven hyperedges supporting a
K_{5}^{(3)}

that do not involve
b^{23}
.

Claim 5.2
.

There exist blue vertices
b^{15}\in\mathfrak{B}^{15}
,
b^{45}\in\mathfrak{B}^{45}
and red vertices
r^{25}\in\mathfrak{R}^{25}
,

r^{35}\in\mathfrak{R}^{35}
such that
b^{12}b^{15}r^{25}
,
r^{13}b^{15}r^{35}
,
r^{14}b^{15}b^{45}
,
r^{24}r^{25}b^{45}
, and
b^{34}r^{35}b^{45}
are hyperedges in
\mathcal{A}
.

Proof.

We consider two sets of “candidates” for the pair
(b^{15},b^{45})
that are
relevant for the existence of
r^{25}
and
r^{35}
. More precisely, we set

\displaystyle G_{1}

\displaystyle=\{(B^{15},B^{45})\in\mathfrak{B}^{15}\times\mathfrak{B}^{45}\colon N_{\mathfrak{R}^{25}}(b^{12},B^{15})\cap N_{\mathfrak{R}^{25}}(r^{24},B^{45})\neq\varnothing\}

\displaystyle\quad\text{and}\quad G_{2}

\displaystyle=\{(B^{15},B^{45})\in\mathfrak{B}^{15}\times\mathfrak{B}^{45}\colon N_{\mathfrak{R}^{35}}(r^{13},B^{15})\cap N_{\mathfrak{R}^{35}}(b^{34},B^{45})\neq\varnothing\}\,.

Note that for every
B^{15}\in\mathfrak{B}^{15}
there is some

R^{25}\in N_{\mathfrak{R}^{25}}(b^{12},B^{15})
and we have

|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{45}}(r^{24},R^{25})|\overset{\eqref{eq:codegreeR}}{\geq}\frac{1}{3\beta}|\mathfrak{B}^{45}|\,.

Clearly,
\{B^{15}\}\times N_{\mathfrak{B}^{45}}(r^{24},R^{25})\subseteq G_{1}
and, hence, we establish

(5.7)

\displaystyle|G_{1}|\geq\frac{1}{3\beta}|\mathfrak{B}^{15}||\mathfrak{B}^{45}|\,.

A symmetric argument yields the same bound for
G_{2}
. Combining (
5.7
)
and the same bound for
G_{2}
with (
5.4
) leads to

\displaystyle|G_{1}|+|G_{2}|+|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{15}\times\mathfrak{B}^{45}}(r^{14})|\geq\left(\frac{2}{3\beta}+\frac{1}{3\varrho}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)|\mathfrak{B}^{15}||\mathfrak{B}^{45}|\overset{\eqref{eq:rhobeta}}{>}2\,|\mathfrak{B}^{15}||\mathfrak{B}^{45}|\,.

Consequently, we can fix a pair
(b^{15},b^{45})\in G_{1}\cap G_{2}\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{15}\times\mathfrak{B}^{45}}(r^{14})
.
Moreover, having fixed
b^{15}
and
b^{45}
this yields a vertex
r^{25}\in\mathfrak{R}^{25}
from the non-empty intersection considered in the definition of
G_{1}
. Similarly,
G_{2}
leads to our choice of
r^{35}\in\mathfrak{R}^{35}
.

Since
(b^{15},b^{45})\in N_{\mathfrak{B}^{15}\times\mathfrak{B}^{45}}(r^{14})
,
the hyperedge
r^{14}b^{15}b^{45}
exists in
\mathcal{A}
and the other four
hyperedges result from the definitions of
G_{1}
and
G_{2}
.
∎

As mentioned above, Claims
5.1
and
5.2
fix all vertices
except
b^{23}\in\mathfrak{B}^{23}
and all hyperedges not involving
b^{23}
.
For the three remaining hyperedges it suffices to show that

N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(b^{12},r^{13})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{25},r^{35})\neq\varnothing\,.

Claim
5.1

( )
‣
5.1
and (
5.2
) imply

\big|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(b^{12},r^{13})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{25},r^{35})\big|\\
\geq\big|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(b^{12},r^{13})\cap N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{24},b^{34})\big|+\big|N_{\mathfrak{B}^{23}}(r^{25},r^{35})\big|-\big|\mathfrak{B}^{23}\big|\\
\overset{\eqref{eq:codegreeR}}{\geq}\left(1-\frac{1}{3\beta}+\frac{1}{3\beta}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}-1\right)|\mathfrak{B}^{23}|>0\,.

Hence a suitable choice for
b^{23}
exists and, therefore,
\mathcal{A}
restricted to
J
supports a
K_{5}^{(3)}
.
∎

Concluding Remarks

We close with a few related open problems and possible directions for future research.

Obtaining sharp bounds for
R(3;r)
is a well known open problem in Ramsey theory.
The aforementioned upper bound on
R(3;r)
together with the work of Schur
[
17
]

yields

2^{\Omega(r)}\leq R(3;r)\leq 2^{O(r\log r)}\,.

The intriguing problem of deciding whether
\displaystyle{\lim_{r\longrightarrow\infty}}R(3;r)^{1/r}
is finite or not is attributed to Erdős (see, e.g.,
[
3
]
*Section 2.5). In case this limit would turn out to be finite, then this would yield
a sharper estimate for (
6.2
). In fact, this would close the gap to (
6.1
) and
the resolution of Problem
6.2
would be
1-\pi_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{1.2}{$\displaystyle\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{225710}{197518}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.0pt}{$\displaystyle\hbox{\hbox to71.99pt{\vbox to63pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 34.7995pt\lower-24.38501pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {

6.2.
Turán problems for hypergraphs with uniformly dense links

As discussed in the introduction there is a small difference between Theorem
1.3

and Corollary
1.5
. Below we briefly elaborate on these differences.
